task:
Parse ONE workplace policy into exactly ONE typed semantic structure.
Field rules:
- modality: PERMISSION (the text grants or allows), PROHIBITION (the text forbids or bars), REQUIREMENT (the text obliges).
- relation: how the regulated act is gated.
  IF: when the conditions hold the act is licensed/obligated/forbidden; when they do not hold the text stays silent (NOT a violation, and NOT permission).
  ONLY_IF: exclusive - the act is licensed ONLY under the conditions; doing it without them is a VIOLATION.
  IF_AND_ONLY_IF: the act is licensed exactly under the conditions and the text commits in both directions.
  UNLESS: the conditions are exceptions carved out of an otherwise absolute rule.
  UNCONDITIONAL: no conditions stated.
  AND_NOT_EACH: doing BOTH targets together is forbidden; each alone is allowed.
- target_clauses: a list of clauses; each clause is a list of atoms that are regulated TOGETHER (same act or same batch); several clauses mean the atoms are regulated SEPARATELY.
- condition_literals and exception_literals: typed atoms copied EXACTLY from atom_catalog; prefix an atom with "!" only when the text negates it.
- condition_mode/exception_mode: ALL means conjunction (every literal), ANY means disjunction (any literal).
- temporal: BEFORE or AFTER only when the text orders the act relative to an event, else NONE.
- WHO is allowed or forbidden to act (for example "only the duty engineer") goes into condition_literals as an actor: atom from atom_catalog; the actor field stays "assistant".
- An act that is neither licensed nor forbidden is NO_VIOLATION, never PERMITTED: absence of prohibition is NOT permission.
Use ONLY atoms from atom_catalog (it also contains distractor atoms; choose the ones the text actually uses). Output exactly one JSON object matching the schema.
